skill.name: run-tests
skill.description: Run Catalyst-Relay unit tests, Node import checks, and SAP integration test workflows when verifying code changes.
skill.summary: Guides repeatable Catalyst-Relay test verification across unit, import, and SAP integration workflows.
skill.author: Artisan-Edge

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown backtick false positives in examples and tables. The SAP integration workflow contains real risks because it passes SAP_PASSWORD to test.bat and can exercise live SAP workflows. No evidence of prompt injection was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: SAP password is passed as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secret prompt or protected environment variable instead. Mask the value in logs and avoid writing it to output files.

remediation.issue: Integration tests connect to a live SAP system.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of a non-production target and least-privilege test credentials before running integration tests.

remediation.issue: The local batch script behavior is not described.
remediation.suggestion: Document what test.bat runs, what files it reads or writes, and how users can inspect it before execution.

remediation.issue: Environment template handling is not bounded.
remediation.suggestion: Ensure .env.templ contains placeholders only and warn users never to commit real SAP credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Passed as Command Argument
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks the user to run test.bat with SAP_PASSWORD and documents that password as passed to the script. Command-line secrets can leak through history, process metadata, or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command instruction and environment table directly connect SAP_PASSWORD to a command argument. This is a well-known credential exposure pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Live SAP Integration Test Side Effects
semantic_findings.description: The integration workflow connects to a live SAP system and covers object lifecycle, CRAUD, table, search, and data preview tests. These tests may modify or expose enterprise data if run against production or broad credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file states that integration tests require live SAP credentials and lists lifecycle and CRAUD coverage. The exact side effects depend on the target SAP system.

content.value_statement: Developers need repeatable test steps before changing Catalyst-Relay. This skill guides unit checks, Node import validation, and SAP integration test review.
actual_capabilities: Guides full Bun unit test runs for the Catalyst-Relay project.
Shows how to run tests in watch mode during active development.
Provides a Node import compatibility check before publishing.
Outlines the SAP integration test workflow and required variables.
Maps named workflow tests to SAP and ABAP feature coverage.
limitations: It is specific to the Catalyst-Relay repository structure.
SAP integration tests require valid live system credentials.
It does not guarantee that the target SAP system is safe for testing.
It currently documents password passing through a command argument.

use_cases.title: Verify a Feature Change
use_cases.description: Run the standard unit test flow after modifying Catalyst-Relay code.

use_cases.title: Check Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm unit tests and Node import validation before publishing a package update.

use_cases.title: Review SAP Workflow Coverage
use_cases.description: Understand which integration tests cover ABAP, CDS, discovery, search, and preview workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run Unit Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the standard unit test workflow for this project and summarize any failures by file.

prompt_templates.title: Focus Test Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the relevant focused tests for my recent change and explain failing assertions in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Publishing Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Run unit tests, perform the Node import compatibility check, and report whether the package is ready to publish.

prompt_templates.title: Assess SAP Integration Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the required SAP test variables, ask before any credentialed action, and review the completed test output for workflow failures.

output_examples.input: Run the project tests after my change.
output: Unit tests completed with two failures.
Both failures relate to workflow validation after the recent change.
Next action: inspect the failing assertions before rerunning the focused tests.

output_examples.input: Check whether this is ready to publish.
output: The Node import validation completed successfully.
The package appears ready for release from the documented checks.

output_examples.input: Review the SAP integration test output.
output: The integration run reached the live SAP test target.
The ABAP class workflow failed during update validation.
Use a non-production system before rerunning credentialed tests.

best_practices: Run unit tests before committing or publishing project changes.
Use a non-production SAP tenant with least-privilege test credentials.
Keep passwords out of command history, logs, and shared output files.
anti_patterns: Passing real SAP passwords as command-line arguments.
Running integration tests against production without explicit approval.
Treating a successful import check as full test coverage.

faq.question: What project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is written for Catalyst-Relay and its documented Bun, Node, and SAP integration test workflow.

faq.question: Can it run all tests automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide unit test execution. SAP integration testing requires credentials and explicit user control.

faq.question: Does it need SAP credentials?
faq.answer: Only the integration workflow needs SAP credentials. Unit tests and import validation do not require them.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with production SAP?
faq.answer: No. Use a non-production SAP system because integration tests may modify or read live objects.

faq.question: Does it replace release testing?
faq.answer: No. It covers documented checks, but teams should keep their normal release gates.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
